description: Accelerates floating-point matrix multiplication with a constant-time 2-element dot product and accumulate instruction.

instructions.name: fdot2_custom
instructions.pseudocode:
a0 = in[0]
a1 = in[1]
b0 = in[2]
b1 = in[3]
c = in[4]
p0 = ftz(a0 * b0)
p1 = ftz(a1 * b1)
s0 = ftz(c + p0)
res = ftz(s0 + p1)
out[0] = res
out[1] = 0
out[2] = 0
out[3] = 0
out[4] = 0
rd = 0
instructions.semantics: The instruction operates on an input memory block of 5 words pointed to by rs1, and an output memory block of 5 words pointed to by rs2. The input block contains five 32-bit floats: a0, a1, b0, b1, and c, in that order. The instruction flushes any subnormal input values to zero, and computes the dot product and addition: res = c + (a0 * b0) + (a1 * b1). It performs independent multiplications and additions with intermediate flush-to-zero and standard round-to-nearest rounding (not a fused multiply-add). The 32-bit float result is written to the first word of the output block, with subnormal results flushed to zero. The remaining 4 words of the output block are zero-padded. The instruction writes 0 to the architectural register rd. The hardware implementation is strictly constant-time, taking a fixed number of cycles independent of the operand values, and silently discards all floating-point exceptions.

name: Float Matrix Multiply Extension
